headline: Your blood IGF-1
body: The growth plate makes its own IGF-1 and responds to that.
punch: Which is why the number on your bloodwork is close to meaningless here.

headline: IGF-1 works
body: Growth plate chondrocytes produce IGF-1 themselves and respond to what's made in the tissue next to them. Liver IGF-1 arrives by blood on top of that, but it isn't the main signal at the plate.
punch: The tissue partly supplies its own.

headline: Which is why
body: Growth hormone acts directly on human growth plate stem cells through JAK/STAT and local TGF beta. That was shown in single cell sequencing of human pubertal growth plate biopsies. It bypasses the liver entirely.
punch: The GH to liver to IGF-1 chain is one of two paths, not the path.

headline: GH and IGF-1
body: Infused separately into rats with the pituitary removed, GH recruited resting zone chondrocytes into the proliferative pool. IGF-1 expanded cells already dividing.
punch: GH sets how many start. IGF-1 sets how far each one goes.

headline: So raising serum IGF-1
body: Push it systemically and it rises in every IGF-1 responsive tissue in your body. The dose limit isn't set by the growth plate, it's set by everything else you're also stimulating.
punch: You run out of headroom before the plate is optimal.

headline: Which is why
body: Researchers built cartilage targeted IGF-1 specifically to concentrate the signal where growth happens instead of everywhere at once. That programme only makes sense if systemic levels are insufficient.
punch: The existence of the workaround tells you the problem is real.

headline: The practical read
body: Serum IGF-1 reports liver output. It does not report what concentration your resting zone is sitting in, and those two can move independently.
punch: A normal IGF-1 doesn't mean your plate is well supplied.

headline: And it explains
body: If the limiting factor is local concentration and local receptor availability, adding more circulating hormone stops helping past a point. That's a delivery problem, not a dose problem.
punch: More of a signal that can't reach the tissue changes nothing.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
